title: Internal freeness from a continuous finite lattice-sum presentation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ whose topology is totally disconnected, and $A=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let $X$ be any scheme, $r\geq0$, $J$ any nonempty finite set and $\Lambda_j\subset E^r$ submodules each admitting an $A$-basis whose vectors also form an $E$-basis of $E^r$. For an internal $A_X$-module $Q$, suppose supplied a continuous-function presentation of $Q$ with values in $\sum_j\Lambda_j$ [def-sfb-continuous-function-module-presentation], using the induced topology. Then $Q$ is a finite biproduct of regular internal $A_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Local computation, second paragraph: the sum lattice has a natural free continuous-function sheaf

proof.text: Transport the coefficient subring using continuousIntegers_eq and take the restriction-compatible rank-r continuous-function coordinate equivalences supplied by the continuous lattice sum theorem. Compose their inverses with the given additive presentations and the universe-lift equivalence. The resulting sectionwise coordinate equivalences respect scalar multiplication and restriction.

Use the coordinate maps as the projections of a product fan of unit module sheaves. Its lift sends a tuple of sections to the inverse coordinate map. Additivity and scalar compatibility make the lift linear, and naturality makes it a sheaf morphism. The coordinate equivalences prove the fan equations and uniqueness. This constructs an isomorphism from the encoded module to the finite product of units.

The coefficient encoding carries the regular internal module to the unit module sheaf and preserves finite biproducts. A finite biproduct is also the finite product in the additive category. Compose the two isomorphisms and use full faithfulness to obtain a finite free presentation of Q. Every step includes r=0 and the empty scheme.

theorem continuousLatticeSum_isFree
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type) [NormedField E]
    [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace E] (X : Scheme.{u}) (r : ℕ)
    (J : Type w) [Finite J] [Nonempty J]
    (L : J → Submodule (continuousIntegers l E) (Fin r → E))
    (hL : ∀ j, ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (continuousIntegers l E) (L j),
      ∃ c : Module.Basis (Fin r) E (Fin r → E), ∀ i, (b i : Fin r → E) = c i)
    (Q : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff l E) X))
    (p : ContinuousFunctionPresentation X (continuousIntegers l E) ↥(⨆ j, L j) Q) :
    Mod.IsFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff l E) X) Q
